requirement.text: It must allow a user to download a backup of their medical information.

initial_eus.title: Backup Download of Medical Information
initial_eus.description: As a user, I want to download a backup of my medical information, so that I can retain my own copy of it.
work_items: The system shall allow a user to download a backup of their medical information.

analysis.ethical_objective: Ensure users retain control over and access to their own medical information by enabling them to obtain a copy of it.

obligations.text: The system must enable a user to download a backup of their medical information.
obligations.source_span: It must allow a user to download a backup of their medical information.

constraints: The downloadable backup pertains to the user's own medical information.
ambiguities: The scope of 'medical information' (e.g., which records or data categories are included) is not specified.
The format, structure, or completeness of the 'backup' is not specified.
The term 'user' is not further defined (e.g., patient, caregiver, or other role).
unsupported_assumptions_to_avoid: Do not assume a specific file format, encryption, or delivery mechanism for the backup.
Do not assume timing, frequency, or scheduling requirements for downloads.
Do not assume authentication, identity verification, or authorization mechanisms beyond what the source states.
Do not assume the backup must be machine-readable, interoperable, or portable to other systems.
Do not assume applicability of specific laws or regulations (e.g., data portability rights).
possible_operational_aspects: The download capability is available to the user.
The backup covers the user's own medical information.

work_items.explanation: The work item directly restates O1: the system enables a user to download a backup of their own medical information, preserving the constraint that the backup pertains to the user's own data.
